judge_assessment.explanation: Both findings check out and the coverage gap runs a little wider. Problem 8 ends 'What fraction of the bar is shaded altogether? Is the bar completely full? Explain using the bar.' and verify.json id 8 is a single `eval` -> 5/6; problem 10 says 'Use a sevenths bar to show why Jae's answer cannot be right, explain in one sentence what Jae did wrong, and write the correct sum' and id 10 is a single `eval` -> 5/7. The file contains no manual entry at all, machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags is false, and final_response.md is written as a fully-verified delivery. The page-count claim is also confirmed: the delivery says '3.5-5 cm of work space per problem, 3 pages' while pdfinfo reports Pages: 5. Beyond the judge's list, problem 5 prints two required responses - 'write it as a fraction, and also say how many whole bars and how many eighths that is' - and id 5 asserts only 9/8, leaving '1 whole and 1 eighth' unchecked; problem 3 says 'Write the difference, then simplify it' and asserts only the simplified 1/3, not the intermediate 3/9. I recomputed all ten answers - 4/5, 7/8, 1/3, 2/3, 9/8, 5/9, 1/2, 5/6, 7/8, 5/7 - and every one matches the key.

strengths_to_preserve: Every bar model is cut into exactly the denominator's number of parts and the student shades or crosses out BEFORE writing the number sentence, with the sentence skeleton printed underneath (problem 1's '1/5 + 3/5 ='). The notation is genuinely read off the picture, which is what the concept-models mode asks for, and the denominators rotate (fifths, eighths, ninths, sixths, twelfths, sevenths) so the model is never decorative.

Problem 9 is the one place on the sheet where a second printed slot IS covered: 'Work backwards' prints the equation blank and the answer line, and the `solve` entry on x - 3/8 - 4/8 returns 7/8, which is what fills both. Typing the missing-number items as `solve` rather than `eval` is the right call and should be kept.

Problem 10's trap is expressed as the misconception itself - (3 + 2)/(7 + 7) - rather than as a typed 5/14, so the number in Jae's stem is derived from the error it represents and the key's grader block cannot drift from the worksheet.

The simplification requirement is placed deliberately rather than uniformly: problems 3, 4 and 7 land on answers that must be reduced (3/9 to 1/3, 4/6 to 2/3, 6/12 to 1/2) while problem 5 deliberately crosses one whole (9/8), so 'keep the denominator' and 'simplify at the end' are taught as separate steps.

root_causes.description: Two problems ask for a written explanation and are recorded as machine-verified, so a concept-models sheet whose last item is an error diagnosis reports zero manual review. SKILL.md already reserves manual for 'any explanation/reasoning answer', but no gate compares a stem's text against the types of the entries filed under it.
evidence: Worksheet problem 8: 'Is the bar completely full? Explain using the bar.' - verify.json id 8 is one `eval` -> 5/6.
Worksheet problem 10: '... explain in one sentence what Jae did wrong ...' - verify.json id 10 is one `eval` -> 5/7.
verify.json contains no entry of type manual; machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags is false.
SKILL.md: 'Use `manual` for: ... and any explanation/reasoning answer.'

root_causes.description: Problems that ask for two numeric forms of the same quantity are verified on one form only, because the coverage gate counts problem ids rather than printed responses. Problem 5's second response ('how many whole bars and how many eighths') and problem 3's intermediate difference are both machine-checkable and both unasserted.
evidence: Worksheet problem 5: 'The sum is bigger than one whole bar - write it as a fraction, and also say how many whole bars and how many eighths that is.' - verify.json id 5 asserts only 9/8.
Worksheet problem 3: 'Write the difference, then simplify it.' - verify.json id 3 asserts only 1/3, not 3/9.
verify.json holds exactly ten entries for ten problems, one per id.

root_causes.description: The delivery's page count is narrated rather than read back from the compiled PDF, so the user is told the worksheet is 3 pages when the file is 5. The build measured the true value during the page-budget gate and it was never carried into the response.
evidence: final_response.md: '3.5-5 cm of work space per problem, 3 pages.'
pdfinfo worksheet.pdf reports Pages: 5; machine_observation.worksheet_pages is 5.
The same misstatement appears in curr-113 and curr-138 in this shard.

improvements.title: Record explanation, diagnosis and drawn-representation responses as manual instead of machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Add the open-response cue gate: fail when a stem contains 'explain', 'why', 'show why', 'in one sentence' or a drawing/shading verb while every entry under that id is a machine type. The fix is a manual companion beside the numeric check. On curr-126 problems 8 and 10 gain companions, the build exits 2 with two manual items, and the delivery reports 10 verified plus 2 manual instead of a silent zero.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: curr-126's problem 10 stem with only its `eval` -> 5/7 entry must fail the new gate and name problem 10; the same fixture with a manual companion must pass with exit 2. Today it passes with exit 0 and no manual tally.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes this case's sole hard failure and the dominant misclassification cluster in the run. A grader learns which two items need a human read.
improvements.risk: Concept-models sheets often use shading as scaffolding rather than as a graded response; firing on every 'shade' cue would over-flag. Restrict the drawing cues to stems where the drawing is the ASKED response ('show why', 'draw and explain') and keep an override.

improvements.title: Require one verification entry (or a manual companion) per printed answer slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Apply the per-slot rule so 'write it as X, and also as Y' items carry an entry per form. On curr-126 id 5 gains a check for the mixed-number form (1 whole and 1 eighth) beside its 9/8, and id 3 gains the unsimplified difference 3/9 beside its 1/3, so the intermediate the worksheet explicitly asks for is asserted rather than assumed.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a problem declaring "slots": 2 whose stem asks for a fraction and a mixed number, supplied with only one entry; assert verify.py exits 1 naming the uncovered slot. Today it exits 0.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the remaining coverage holes on this sheet and, across the run, the largest hard-failure cluster.
improvements.risk: More entries per problem and a longer verification file. The values are already computed by the generator, so the cost is file size rather than authoring effort.

improvements.title: Generate the delivery response's page counts from the compiled PDFs instead of writing them by hand
improvements.proposed_change: Emit the measured page counts from the page-budget gate into gate_log.txt and require the delivery text to quote those numbers. curr-126's response would then say 5 pages, matching the file the user opens.
improvements.regression_test: Assert gate_log.txt contains a machine-readable PAGES line with ws=5 for this fixture and that a response claiming 3 is flagged. The line does not exist today.
improvements.expected_impact: Fixes a repeated credibility defect across the shard at negligible cost.
improvements.risk: Very low; additive to the log and the response text only.

case_summary: A carefully built concept-models sheet: every bar is cut into the denominator's number of parts, the student shades before writing the sentence, the missing-number items are typed `solve` so the blank is what SymPy solves for, and all ten answers recompute correctly. It is rejected because two of those ten problems ask the student to explain - problem 8 'Is the bar completely full? Explain using the bar' and problem 10 'explain in one sentence what Jae did wrong' - and both are recorded as machine-verified, so the sheet reports zero manual items. I also found two printed responses the judge did not: problem 5's 'how many whole bars and how many eighths' and problem 3's unsimplified difference. The judge's minor note is also correct - the delivery calls the worksheet 3 pages when it is 5.
